Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Action bar.

When to use

The action bar is the bottom edge of a pushed screen: where the screen's job is committed. It replaces the tab bar of the screen shell; 87 pages in wireframes/ draw it. Every button in it is filled and full width, stacked one per row. Text-only rungs (tertiary, text) live in the nav bar, never here.

While the onscreen keyboard is up the bar takes [hidden] and leaves; buttons drawn behind the keys while still in the tab order would fail WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured. A screen with nothing to commit ends at </main> and draws no bar: earning-details, notifications, role-select and the four filter screens.

The primary is on top in every action bar (designer, rev 290): the screen's job first, the way out under it, in the markup as well as on screen. Drawers stack Done over Cancel the same way (rev 291); the finder keeps Filters over Find, her own call. Labels name the outcome and state a price before the tap: Pay ₴180, Submit review, Contact support, Try again.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Navigation · voice.md P1, P3 · microcopy.md § Master table · inventory.md § 1 (Action bar)

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Submit report Submit without evidence

report-issue: the main job as the primary, the way out as a secondary under it, each on its own full-width row.

Don’t

You can change this later in Account → Switch role.

A bar that holds no button. role-select's bar carried only this note until the designer removed it; a fact belongs in the column as a message or a lead line, and a screen with no action ends at </main>. For a choice between routes rather than a commitment, use choice cards in the column, not a stack of buttons in the bar.
